summary_paragraph: A 31-year-old woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, asthma, and GERD was admitted for dyspnea and thickened green tracheal secretions. She reported difficulty breathing through her tracheostomy stoma, which she believed had partially closed, and decreased oral fluid intake. Vital signs were stable, and physical exam showed a clean trach site with clear lungs. Lab results were normal, and chest imaging revealed no acute cardiopulmonary abnormalities. She was treated with humidified oxygen, IV fluids for hydration, and guaifenesin to loosen secretions. Symptoms improved significantly by the next morning, and the planned inpatient bronchoscopy was deferred to outpatient follow-up with interventional pulmonology. No medication changes were made during admission. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue current medications and attend scheduled follow-up.
